Design notes for reviewers
  • Facebook accounts (AC9): chosen approach is Option (a) — a Facebook-originated account sets an app-managed password for the first time via this same reset flow, which then coexists with Facebook Login. Alternative considered: an account-unlink/recovery flow, rejected here as more disruptive for a "regain access" story. Needs explicit product sign-off before build — see the callout on the "Set new password" screen (Facebook variant).
  • AC10 / AC16 (no enumeration): the "request sent" confirmation screen shows an identical generic message whether the identifier is registered, unregistered, or has hit the 5-requests/hour cap. See the callout on that screen for what happens silently in each case.
  • AC15 (mutual invalidation): the "Set new password" screen shows a note naming whichever method (link or OTP) was not used, confirming it's now invalid.
  • No dedicated error/success/warning tokens exist in tokens.json — this prototype reuses color-primary for error and color-secondary for success. Flagging in case first-class status tokens are wanted later.

Reviewer aid — pick a scenario, not shown to real users

Check your email and phone

If the identifier you entered matches a registered account, we've sent a password reset link to the email on file and a 6-digit one-time code by SMS. Both are valid for a limited time.

Didn't get anything? Check your spam folder, or wait a few minutes and try again.

Design note (AC10): this identifier isn't tied to any account. The message above is identical to the registered case on purpose — no email or SMS is actually sent, but the user can't tell that from the UI, so account existence isn't leaked.
Design note (AC16): this identifier already had 5 reset requests in the past hour. The same generic confirmation is shown, but no new link or OTP is issued for this request — the previously issued ones (if still valid) remain the only usable ones.
